lessons.text: Never use no true scotsman (Redefining a category on the fly to exclude a damaging counterexample). It cost you against Benjamin Franklin.
Never use ad hominem (Attacking the arguer instead of the argument). It cost you against Benjamin Franklin.

Prepare an answer before you assert: Benjamin Franklin broke through with "But note what just happened: your argument skipped the evidence entirely. The research found the effect repeatedly; since the premise survi…" (Clean argument. structure=0.50, evidence=1.00).

Prepare an answer before you assert: Benjamin Franklin broke through with "However, your premise assumes what it needs to prove, and the data shows otherwise. The research found the effect repeatedly; since the pre…" (Clean argument. structure=0.50, evidence=1.00).

Borrow this pattern from Benjamin Franklin: "But note what just happened: your argument skipped the evidence entirely. The research found the effect repeatedly; since the premise survi…" — it carried evidence, its premises led cleanly to the conclusion.

Your weakest move against Benjamin Franklin was "However, your premise assumes what it needs to prove, and the data shows otherwise. The research found the effect repeatedly; since the pre…" (soundness 0.20). State its premises and evidence before you use it again.
